issues.description: The problem statement/UML and the reference solution define the main farm class as `Farm`, but the template file `src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java` declares `public class AnimalFarm`. This name mismatch prevents students from following the instructions/UML directly and will cause mismatches with any references expecting a `Farm` class.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template's `AnimalFarm` class to `Farm` (and ensure the file remains `Farm.java` with `public class Farm`). Update any TODO comments accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement/UML and the reference solution require the helper method `singFarmSongVerse` to accept an `Animal` parameter (`singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)`), but the template declares `private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)` with the parameter commented out. This prevents implementing the verse logic as specified because the method has no way to access the current animal.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template signature to `private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)` and ensure `Animal` is available in the same package (or imported if needed).

issues.description: The template `src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java` is syntactically corrupted: it contains a second `package de.tum.cit.ase;` declaration and a second `public class AnimalFarm { ... }` nested inside the `singFarmSong()` method body. This makes the starter project uncompilable, blocking any student work regardless of intended TODO stubs.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the template `Farm.java` with a single valid compilation unit: one `package` line, one top-level `public class Farm` (or the intended class), and only the intended method stubs/TODOs (no nested duplicate class or package declaration).
